topics.topic: Whether an existing StoredValue identity should raise StoreInternalError or be reused and returned
questions: Must an existing StoredValue identity raise StoreInternalError as an existing identity for an immutable record, or is StoredValue the exception that must be reused and returned?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1, and neither the relevant text nor its quoted passages has changed.

precedent.topic: Whether record_change should reject or reuse an existing equal StoredValue identity
quotes: A StoredValue whose value_id already exists is not written again and the existing record is returned in its place, since equal values share one identity; spooled files must already be published in the run's spool by spool_file before the change that writes their SpooledFile records.

Any other broken invariant (a linked record missing, an identity already present for an immutable record, a status change from a status the change does not start from) or a failed transaction raises StoreInternalError with nothing written.
precedent.why: The specific StoredValue rule requires returning the existing record without rewriting it, while the phrase “Any other broken invariant” excludes that stated special case.

topics.topic: Final run status when an execution is refused by the owner and nothing waits
questions: Must a run containing a refused_by_owner execution end refused, or does the failed-otherwise rule make it failed when nothing waits?

judgement.why: This asks the same final-status question for a refused_by_owner execution on unchanged text.

precedent.topic: Final run status when an execution is refused_by_owner
quotes: If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused.
precedent.why: The terminal status is explicitly refused.

topics.topic: Whether size/token failures must read and parse the body to preserve the request id
questions: For a size or token failure, must the body remain unread, or must it be parsed to preserve a valid string or integer id?
For a request rejected by the size check, must the body remain unread, or must it be read to preserve a string or integer id in the error response?

judgement.why: This asks the same unchanged question about body parsing and response-id recovery already answered by P7.

precedent.topic: Whether size or token refusals must leave the body unread with a null id or may parse it to recover the id
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.

topics.topic: Precedence and scope of serve_kernel checks for origin, route, method, and request size
questions: What status must be returned when a request both carries an Origin header and uses another method on the endpoint or another path?
Must every oversized request reach answer_request, or only an oversized POST to the configured path without an Origin header?

quotes: Only a POST to the path equal to the imported MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH constant reaches answer_request; any other method on that path is answered 405, any other path 404, and a request carrying an Origin header 403, each without a body and without calling answer_request; no Mcp-Session-Id header is ever sent, one presented is ignored, and no event stream is opened.

MUST read at most one byte more of a request body than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SURFACE_REQUEST_BYTES_MAX constant allows, so an oversized request still reaches answer_request and is refused there;
judgement.why: Origin always produces 403, and only a POST to the configured path reaches answer_request, so the oversized-body forwarding rule applies only to such a routed request without an Origin header.

topics.topic: Whether reached-handler internal errors are propagated or returned as isError results
questions: When a reached handler raises an exception that translate_failure maps to internal_error, must answer_request propagate it or return it as an isError tool result?

quotes: MUST call the handler of the named operation, whose name is handle_ followed by the operation name — exactly one of handle_accept_binding, handle_activate_flow_version, handle_add_trial_case, handle_cancel_run, handle_capture_failed_execution, handle_compose_flow_version, handle_decide_effect_approval, handle_get_binding, handle_get_contract_version, handle_get_flow, handle_get_flow_version, handle_get_implementation, handle_get_repair_view, handle_get_run, handle_get_slot, handle_grant_standing_approval, handle_issue_contract_version, handle_list_records, handle_propose_binding, handle_prove_flow_version, handle_read_fixture_file, handle_read_spooled_file, handle_release_run, handle_resolve_unknown_outcome, handle_resume_run, handle_revoke_standing_approval, handle_roll_back_slot, handle_start_run, handle_submit_implementation and handle_try_implementation — with the Actor and the validated request, encode its answer as the tool result — values as JSON text, file bytes as base64 — and turn any exception the handler raises into a refusal answer through translate_failure, except any failure translate_failure answers internal_error — StopRequiredError, StoreInternalError or any unexpected exception, whatever the handler — which it lets propagate to serve_kernel unchanged, since a store change may already be written and only the next start derives every run again.

When answer_request raises StopRequiredError or any other failure it let propagate because its answer is internal_error, MUST first send that request the internal_error answer built by translate_failure, without detail, and then end the process with a non-zero exit code, so the next start derives every run that has not ended (A03 rule 7, A14 rules 5 and 7).
judgement.why: A reached-handler failure mapped to internal_error propagates unchanged to serve_kernel, which sends the internal_error response and then terminates serving.
